subject: Priv deploy packaging and ops credit model
messages:
From: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@helixhealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Priv deploy packaging questions

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the performance profiles for the private stack. Before we move to an SOW, procurement asked I clarify a few things about packaging and ops credits so we can model cost into the Q3 budget: 

1) License unit framing — are you able to confirm whether the on-prem offering is sold per-operator license (named seats for admins/SRE) + site entitlements, or per-GPU/node capacity? We have a mixed edge+core footprint and want to avoid double-charging.

2) Platform fee amortization — we typically capitalize platform fees over 3–5 quarters. Do you offer an annualized option or a pilot discount to amortize the platform fee across the first 12 months?

3) SRE retainer vs on-call credits — our internal ops prefers a small retainer and then credits for bursts. Can you describe how the burst credit works (granularity, invoice offsets, burn rules)?

4) Escrow & compliance addendum — a quick ask: does Redwood support code escrow or a custodian for binaries for regulated customers?

Attached is a first-pass environment document (Helix_Initial_SOW.xlsx) that shows expected VM/GPU counts. If you can send a short matrix of packaging options and an example amortization schedule we can run this through procurement.

Appreciate it —
Sarah
Sarah Bennett
Program Manager, Platform Investments
HelixHealth

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@helixhealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priv deploy packaging questions

Hi Sarah — thanks, and great to hear the demo landed well. Putting answers below and attaching a short term matrix (redwood_privdeploy_term_matrix.pdf) to make it easier for procurement. Quick TL;DR: we support both node-based licensing and site entitlements; platform fee can be annualized or amortized; burst credits are pre-funded buckets that invoice-credits against monthly usage. Details follow.

— License unit framing (options) —
* Node-based (preferred for predictable GPU-count customers): a node SKU covers the inference runtime for X GPUs. Operators (SRE/admin) are licensed separately as named seats (small per-seat fee). Ideal when customers want usage-aligned pricing.
* Site-entitlement (preferred for multisite customers): a flat site entitlement + per-token consumption. Good for customers who want a single predictable bill across many small edge sites.

We recommend node-based for Helix given the VM/GPU counts in your attachment — it avoids paying for full-site entitlements on low-util edge nodes while keeping a single seat fee for control plane admins.

— Platform fee amortization —
Options: (a) Annualized: invoice one platform fee, then we provide an amortization schedule (12 or 24 mo) + optional pilot discount (one-off 25% credit on month 1); (b) Quarterly commits: reduce platform fee in exchange for a 6–12 month commit. I attached an example table showing a 12-mo amortization with a pilot-month 25% credit.

— SRE retainer vs burst credits —
* Retainer: monthly on-call retainer that covers up to N incidents / monthly SLA response window.
* Burst credits: pre-purchased credit units (e.g., 100 incident-credits) that are consumed when we exceed retainer thresholds or for large migrations. Each credit reduces the bill for on-call SRE time and/or compensates for engineering uplift. Credits expire 12 months after purchase; unused credits roll into a 3-month grace pool for planned migrations.

— Escrow & compliance —
We support an escrow addendum for regulated customers; binaries and a minimal support snapshot can be escrowed with a certified custodian. We'll need a standard NDA and a compliance review to scope what goes to escrow.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll share a short commercial matrix and an amortization sample (attached).
2) If acceptable, we can do a one-page commercial term sheet and a DocuSign stub for the pilot month + amortization schedule.
3) Internal ops (David/priyom) can propose SRE retainer bands and credit quantities for the SOW.

If you want, we can join procurement call next week to walk the matrix.

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_privdeploy_term_matrix.pdf (PDF, 46KB)
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priv deploy packaging questions

Adding some commercial guardrails from the infra/ops side — cc'ing David:

Jasmine / David — below are three commercial scenarios we can offer Helix with suggested SRE retainer and burst-credit mechanics. I focused on minimizing up-front platform fee pressure while keeping some committed economics.

1) Pilot-to-Annual (low friction) — 3-mo pilot: 25% off platform fee first month, amortize remaining platform fee over 12 months. SRE: $8k/mo retainer covering 6hr SLA incidents; burst credits sold in 100-credit buckets @ $750/bucket (each credit ~ 30m of engineering time).

2) Commit-Discount (volume-first) — 12-month commit: 15% platform fee discount, reduced per-node license by 10%. SRE: $12k/mo retainer with 10 incident coverage; burst credits larger buckets @ $2,000 / 300 credits; credits roll for 6 months.

3) Enterprise Foundation (conservative) — multi-site entitlements: higher platform fee but lower per-token charge; SRE: annual retainer + guaranteed priority SLA; burst credits priced at marginal cost.

Operational constraints / billing notes:
* Credits must be purchased in advance and are invoiced as prepaid line items.
* Refunds: we do not typically refund used credits; we can grant one-time goodwill credit for exceptional migration events.
* Escrow: add-on cost — range $15k–$40k depending on packaging and frequency of snapshots.

If Helix wants to keep capital spend low, recommendation is scenario 1 with a modest retainer + pre-funded small credit bucket. We can draft an SOW appendix with explicit credit burn rules and examples.

Let me know if folks want numbers tightened and I’ll prepare a short workbook.

— Priyom
Principal Commercial Engineer
Redwood Inference

Jasmine — thanks for the fast turn. The matrix and scenarios are exactly what procurement wanted. A few quick clarifications before we route to legal: 

1) For scenario 1 (Pilot-to-Annual) — can you confirm the amortization invoice schedule (we prefer equal monthly amortization with a single pilot credit applied to month 1)?
2) For burst credits — will usage be visible in the Console token-level dashboard so we can forecast burn?
3) Escrow — confirm the mid-range estimate ($25k) to budget for the Q3 request.

Also — procurement asked if Redwood will provide a 10% introductory concession on the platform fee if we sign the pilot SOW this month. It’s not a deal-breaker, but would speed approvals.

If you can send a one-page commercial term sheet and the DocuSign stub, we can route this Thursday.

Thanks —
Sarah
